topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its core learning objectives.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Therapies and Limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine conventional methods for removing or destroying tumors alongside the clinical challenges of non-specific toxicity and acquired resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cancer Cell Vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that selectively eliminate tumor cells by exploiting their intrinsic genetic and physiological defects.

topics.label: Targeting Oncogenic Kinases and Mechanisms of Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on small-molecule inhibitors directed against hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and the molecular mechanisms causing therapeutic resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Antibody-Based Targeted Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the use of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to specifically deliver cytotoxic effects against tumor cell surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine approaches that mobilize and re-engineer the host immune system to recognize and destroy tumor cells.

topics.label: Challenges, Progress, and Future Directions in Cancer Management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broad systemic challenges, historical improvements in survival, and emerging considerations for future cancer care.
